mill_linear.title: Linear Milling (G01)
mill_linear.description: Move the tool in a straight line at programmed feedrate
mill_linear.example:
O0001 (LINEAR MILLING EXAMPLE)
N10 G90 G54 G17 G20 (Absolute, WCS, XY plane, Inch)
N20 G00 X0 Y0 (Rapid to start)
N30 G43 H01 Z0.5 (Tool length comp, safe Z)
N40 S3000 M03 (Spindle on 3000 RPM CW)
N50 G00 Z0.1 (Rapid to clearance)
N60 G01 Z-0.25 F10.0 (Feed to depth)
N70 G01 X2.0 F20.0 (Linear cut to X2)
N80 G01 Y2.0 (Linear cut to Y2)
N90 G01 X0 (Linear cut back)
N100 G01 Y0 (Complete square)
N110 G00 Z0.5 (Retract)
N120 M05 (Spindle off)
N130 G28 G91 Z0 (Return home Z)
N140 M30 (End program)
tips: G01 is modal - stays active until changed
F-word is also modal - set once, used until changed
Use G90 for absolute, G91 for incremental moves
Always approach from a safe Z height first

mill_arc.title: Arc/Circular Interpolation (G02/G03)
mill_arc.description: Move tool in a circular arc - CW (G02) or CCW (G03)

parameters.desc: Incremental X distance to arc center
Incremental Y distance to arc center

mill_arc.example:
O0002 (ARC MILLING EXAMPLE)
N10 G90 G54 G17 G20
N20 G00 X0 Y-1.0
N30 G43 H01 Z0.5
N40 S2500 M03
N50 G00 Z0.1
N60 G01 Z-0.125 F10.0

(Arc using R - simpler)
N70 G02 X1.0 Y0 R1.0 F15.0 (CW 90° arc, R=1)

(Arc using I,J - more precise)
N80 G03 X0 Y1.0 I-1.0 J0 F15.0 (CCW arc)

(Full circle - must use I,J)
N90 G02 I0 J-1.0 F12.0 (Full CW circle)

N100 G00 Z0.5
N110 M30
tips: G02 = Clockwise, G03 = Counter-clockwise (in G17 XY plane)
R method: positive R for arcs ≤180°, negative for >180°
I,J method: incremental distance FROM start TO center
Full circles MUST use I,J (R cannot define 360°)
Plane selection matters: G17=XY, G18=XZ, G19=YZ

mill_helix.title: Helical Interpolation
mill_helix.description: Combine circular motion with Z-axis motion for helical ramping

parameters.desc: End depth (adds Z motion to arc)

mill_helix.example:
O0003 (HELICAL BORE EXAMPLE)
(Mill a 1.0" dia hole using 0.5" endmill)
N10 G90 G54 G17 G20
N20 G00 X0 Y0 (Hole center)
N30 G43 H01 Z0.5
N40 S4000 M03
N50 G00 X0.25 Y0 Z0.1 (Offset by tool radius)

(Helical ramp down - 0.050" per revolution)
N60 G03 X0.25 Y0 Z-0.05 I-0.25 J0 F12.0
N70 G03 X0.25 Y0 Z-0.10 I-0.25 J0
N80 G03 X0.25 Y0 Z-0.15 I-0.25 J0
(Continue until full depth...)
N90 G03 X0.25 Y0 Z-0.50 I-0.25 J0

(Spring pass at full depth)
N100 G03 X0.25 Y0 Z-0.50 I-0.25 J0

N110 G00 Z0.5
N120 M30
tips: Great for ramping into pockets without plunging
Helix diameter = tool path diameter, not final hole size
Keep helix angle <3° for most materials
Add spring pass at bottom for size accuracy

drill_simple.title: Simple Drilling (G81)
drill_simple.description: Basic drill cycle - rapid down, feed to depth, rapid out
drill_simple.example:
O0010 (G81 DRILLING EXAMPLE)
N10 G90 G54 G17 G20
N20 T01 M06 (0.250 Drill)
N30 G43 H01 Z1.0
N40 S2000 M03
N50 G00 X1.0 Y1.0 (First hole position)

N60 G99 G81 X1.0 Y1.0 Z-0.5 R0.1 F8.0
(G99 = return to R plane between holes)
(Drill first hole)

N70 X2.0 (Second hole - only X changes)
N80 X3.0 Y2.0 (Third hole)
N90 Y3.0 (Fourth hole)

N100 G80 (Cancel canned cycle!)
N110 G00 Z1.0
N120 M30
tips: G98 returns to initial Z, G99 returns to R plane
Always G80 to cancel cycle when done!
After first G81, just program X,Y for subsequent holes
R-plane should be 0.1" above work surface
Good for shallow holes up to 3x diameter

drill_peck.title: Peck Drilling (G83)
drill_peck.description: Deep hole drilling with full retract pecks for chip clearing
drill_peck.example:
O0011 (G83 PECK DRILLING)
N10 G90 G54 G17 G20
N20 T01 M06 (0.375 Drill)
N30 G43 H01 Z1.0
N40 S1800 M03
N50 M08 (Coolant ON - important for deep holes!)

(Peck drill 1.5" deep hole, 0.150" pecks)
N60 G99 G83 X1.0 Y1.0 Z-1.5 R0.1 Q0.15 F6.0

(Additional holes)
N70 X2.0 Y1.0
N80 X3.0 Y1.0

N90 G80 (Cancel cycle)
N100 M09 (Coolant off)
N110 G00 Z1.0
N120 M30
tips: Use for holes deeper than 3x drill diameter
Q value typically 0.5 to 1x drill diameter
Full retract clears chips but increases cycle time
Always use coolant for deep hole drilling
Consider G73 high-speed peck for softer materials

drill_deep.title: High-Speed Peck (G73)
drill_deep.description: Chip-breaking peck with partial retract - faster than G83
drill_deep.example:
O0012 (G73 HIGH-SPEED PECK)
N10 G90 G54 G17 G20
N20 T01 M06 (0.5 Drill)
N30 G43 H01 Z1.0
N40 S1500 M03
N50 M08

(High-speed peck - partial retract ~0.030")
N60 G99 G73 X1.0 Y1.0 Z-1.25 R0.1 Q0.20 F8.0

N70 X2.0
N80 X3.0

N90 G80
N100 G00 Z1.0
N110 M30
tips: Retracts only ~0.030" to break chips (not full retract)
Much faster than G83 for aluminum, brass, plastics
NOT recommended for deep holes in steel/stainless
Good for holes 3-6x diameter in soft materials
Chip evacuation relies on flute geometry

drill_tap.title: Tapping (G84)
drill_tap.syntax: G84 X__ Y__ Z__ R__ F__  (F = RPM × Pitch)
tips: CRITICAL: F = RPM × Pitch (must be exact!)
Use rigid tapping (M29 on some controls) when possible
Reduce RPM 30-50% for blind holes
Thread depth = tap chamfer + full threads needed
Pre-drill size is critical for thread quality

turn_od_rough.title: OD Roughing Cycle (G71)
turn_od_rough.description: Multi-pass OD/ID roughing following programmed profile
turn_od_rough.example:
O0020 (G71 OD ROUGHING)
N10 G50 S2500 (Max RPM limit)
N20 T0101 (OD Rough tool)
N30 G96 S600 M03 (CSS 600 SFM)
N40 G00 X3.1 Z0.1

(G71 two-line format)
N50 G71 U0.100 R0.020
N60 G71 P70 Q110 U0.010 W0.005 F0.012

(Profile definition - finish contour)
N70 G00 X0.8
N80 G01 Z0 F0.006
N90 X1.0 Z-0.1 (Chamfer)
N100 Z-1.5
N110 X2.5

(End of G71 cycle)
N120 G00 X5.0 Z2.0
N130 M30
tips: Profile (P-Q) defines the FINISH shape
G71 automatically calculates all roughing passes
U (finish) is diameter value, not radius
Profile must go from small to large diameter
Follow with G70 for finish pass

turn_od_finish.title: Finishing Cycle (G70)
turn_od_finish.description: Single finish pass following G71/G72/G73 profile
turn_od_finish.example:
(After G71 roughing...)
N120 T0202 (Finish tool)
N130 G96 S800 M03
N140 G00 X3.1 Z0.1

(G70 follows same profile as G71)
N150 G70 P70 Q110

N160 G00 X5.0 Z2.0
N170 M30
tips: Uses same P-Q blocks as roughing cycle
F and S in profile blocks ARE used by G70
Change to finish tool before G70
Increase SFM for better finish
No need to re-define profile

turn_thread.title: Threading Cycle (G76)

parameters.desc: 6 digits: passes, spring cuts, infeed angle

turn_thread.example:
O0021 (G76 THREADING - 1.0-8 UNC)
N10 T0303 (Threading tool)
N20 G97 S400 M03 (Constant RPM for threading!)
N30 G00 X1.2 Z0.2

(Thread data: 1.0-8 UNC)
(OD = 1.000, Minor = 0.8466)
(Depth = (1.0-0.8466)/2 = 0.0767")

(G76 two-line format)
N40 G76 P020060 Q0050 R0.001
(P = 02 passes min, 00 spring cuts, 60° infeed)
(Q = 0.0005" min cut, R = 0.001" finish)

N50 G76 X0.8466 Z-1.25 P0767 Q0200 F0.125
(X = minor dia, P = depth×10000)
(Q = first cut 0.020", F = 1/8 = 0.125)

N60 G00 X2.0 Z1.0
N70 M30
tips: MUST use G97 constant RPM (not CSS)
Thread depth P is in 0.0001" units (radius)
Infeed angle: 29-30° for UN, 27.5° for metric
First cut Q should be about 0.020-0.030"
Add spring passes for better finish

turn_groove.title: OD/ID Grooving (G75)
turn_groove.description: Peck grooving cycle for OD or ID grooves
turn_groove.example:
O0022 (G75 GROOVING)
N10 T0505 (0.125 wide groove tool)
N20 G97 S600 M03
N30 G00 X2.1 Z-0.5 (Position at groove start)

(Groove 0.125 wide × 0.25 deep)
N40 G75 R0.010
N50 G75 X1.5 Z-0.625 P0500 Q1250 F0.002
(P = 0.050" peck, Q = 0.125" step = tool width)

N60 G00 X3.0 Z2.0
N70 M30
tips: Tool width defines minimum Q step
P peck depth typically 0.030-0.060"
Use G97 constant RPM for grooving
Low feedrate (0.001-0.003 IPR) for grooving
Retract R clears chips between pecks

turn_simple.title: Simple OD/ID Cycle (G90)
turn_simple.example:
O0023 (G90 SIMPLE TURNING)
N10 T0101
N20 G96 S500 M03
N30 G00 X2.1 Z0.05

(Multiple passes using G90)
N40 G90 X1.8 Z-2.0 F0.012
N50 X1.6
N60 X1.4
N70 X1.2
N80 X1.0

N90 G00 X3.0 Z2.0
N100 M30
tips: G90 is modal - just change X for next pass
Simpler than G71 for basic straight turning
Good for simple diameters without contours
Can add taper with X and Z together
Less efficient than G71 for complex shapes

turn_parting.title: Parting / Cutoff
turn_parting.description: Cut off finished part from bar stock
turn_parting.example:
O0024 (PARTING OFF)
N10 T0404 (Parting tool, 0.118" wide)
N20 G97 S500 M03 (Constant RPM!)
N30 G00 X2.1 Z-2.5 (Position at part-off location)

(Part off with pecking)
N40 G01 X1.8 F0.002
N50 G00 X2.0 (Retract to clear chips)
N60 G01 X1.4 F0.002
N70 G00 X2.0
N80 G01 X1.0 F0.002
N90 G00 X2.0
N100 G01 X0.05 F0.001 (Final cut - leave small pip)
(Or use G75 peck grooving cycle)

N110 G00 X3.0 Z2.0
N120 M30

Very low feed: 0.001-0.003 IPR
Peck to clear chips and prevent tool breakage
Leave small pip (0.02-0.05") to prevent grabbing
Part catcher or hand catch at low RPM for final cut
Consider G75 cycle for automatic pecking

face.title: Face Milling
face.description: Face milling creates a flat surface by moving a face mill or large end mill across the top of the workpiece. The tool removes material in parallel passes, typically with a large stepover (50-70%) for efficiency.
whenToUse: Squaring up material before other operations
Removing saw marks or casting skin

O9100 (BOLT CIRCLE)
(X=CENTER X, Y=CENTER Y, R=RADIUS)
(A=START ANGLE, B=HOLE COUNT, Z=DEPTH, F=FEED)
IF [#18 EQ #0] GOTO99 (NO RADIUS - ERROR)
IF [#2 EQ #0] GOTO99 (NO HOLE COUNT - ERROR)
#100=[#24] (CENTER X)
#101=[#25] (CENTER Y)
#102=[#18] (RADIUS)
#103=[#1] (START ANGLE)
IF [#103 EQ #0] THEN #103=0
#104=[#2] (HOLE COUNT)
#105=[360/#104] (ANGLE INCREMENT)
#106=#104 (LOOP COUNTER)
WHILE [#106 GT 0] DO1
  #107=#100+[#102*COS[#103]]
  #108=#101+[#102*SIN[#103]]
  G81 X#107 Y#108 Z#26 R0.1 F#9
  #103=#103+#105
  #106=#106-1
END1
